sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Nürnberg's car parks are holding up better than Germany's. The same garages were 42–45% occupied on an average day in each year since 2022, and January to September 2026 ran about 2 points above the same months of 2025, while Germany as a whole was 2% down. Covid hit hardest in the second lockdown: occupancy fell to about 26% in the winter of 2020/21, against 39% in April 2020.

The city has been narrowing access to the old town step by step. In 2019 its traffic committee decided to close the Weinmarkt (as a trial), the Bergstraße and the Maxbrücke to cars [0]. The 2021 mobility resolution aims to raise the share of trips on foot, by bike and by public transport from 61% to about 68% by 2030, with fewer parking spaces on the street and more parking in neighbourhood garages [1]. Since February 2022 every formerly free street space in the old town has been paid and time-limited for non-residents [2][3], with the stated aim of moving long-stay parkers into the garages [2]. Street parking in the old town now usually costs €2.50 an hour [11], more than the €2 most central garages charge. Residents' permits stay cheap, because Bavaria kept its cap of €30.70 a year in 2025 [4].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main change in the garage stock has come from department stores. Galeria Kaufhof on Königstraße closed in June 2023 and the city bought the building in 2024 [5]; its 220-space garage reopened in November 2024, run by Goldbeck for the city with plate recognition and cashless payment [6]. In our data it is 36% occupied on weekdays. The garage under Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz was due to pass to a new operator, Park One, once renovation finished in spring 2025 [7].

Nürnberg's energy utility N-ERGIE has made it a test bed for parking technology: a 2019 project planned sensors and charge points for garages outside the centre, with prices that change with traffic and air pollution [9], and its own garage in Sandreuth opened in 2021 with 128 charge points, app reservation and plate recognition [8]. Park-and-ride sites have dozens of charge points and are free with a transit ticket [10]. In the centre, a guidance system shows free spaces in 19 garages with over 5,300 spaces [11].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
The centre is compact and evenly priced. Almost every garage we measure is within a kilometre of the Hauptmarkt, and most charge €2 an hour and €20 a day. The city-owned company Parkhaus Service Nürnberg (PSN) runs most of them, and its garages are among the busier ones (49% on weekdays), with Sterntor at 66%. The busiest garage in town is the one at the main station (74%). The privately run Adlerstraße garage, steps from the Hauptmarkt, is also well used (58%) despite a dearer €30 day ticket. With prices this uniform, price explains nothing about which garages fill.

The central garages are about as busy at weekends as on weekdays, which fits a centre that draws shoppers and visitors more than commuters. City counters recorded 2.6–6.9% more pedestrians on the main shopping streets in 2025 [15], and the transport operator VAG carried a record 160 million passengers in 2024 [14]. Garages tied to department stores and shopping centres are quieter: Karstadt 46%, Galeria 36%, Wöhrl 33%, Sebalder Höfe 26% and the City-Park-Center 11%.
